article.title: Hindi to English: Work context sentence
article.description: Hindi: 'मुझे यह प्रोजेक्ट कल तक पूरा करना है।' English: 'I have to finish this project by tomorrow.' Teaching point: 'करना है' (have to do) is obligation, translated with 'have to' not 'must' here since it's a deadline-driven task obligation, not a personal rule.
article.content: Hindi: 'मुझे यह प्रोजेक्ट कल तक पूरा करना है।' English: 'I have to finish this project by tomorrow.' Teaching point: 'करना है' (have to do) is obligation, translated with 'have to' not 'must' here since it's a deadline-driven task obligation, not a personal rule.

generated.caption:
Got a deadline looming? 🗓️ When you need to express an obligation for a deadline-driven task, 'have to' is your best choice! It clearly shows it's a task with a deadline, not a personal rule. We use 'have to' here, not 'must'.

For example: 'I have to finish this project by tomorrow.'

Save this for later and follow @TheEnglishVault for daily lessons!
generated.script:
मुझे यह प्रोजेक्ट कल तक पूरा करना है — yahan 'have to' aayega ya 'must'? Ye confusion bahut logon ko hota hai na?

Dekho, 'करना है' ka matlab hai obligation. Jab kisi deadline-driven task ki zimmedari ho, use 'have to'. For example, 'मुझे यह प्रोजेक्ट कल तक पूरा करना है।' Isko hum bolenge 'I have to finish this project by tomorrow.' Yahan 'must' use nahi karenge, kyunki ye deadline hai, personal rule nahi.

Toh next time jab task ki obligation ya deadline ho, 'have to' use karna. 'Must' nahi! Clear ho gaya na?

Comment karke batao aapko ye chhoti si tip pehle pata thi ya nahi!

slides.body: Let's translate 'मुझे यह प्रोजेक्ट कल तक पूरा करना है.' which correctly becomes 'I have to finish this project by tomorrow.' The Hindi phrase 'करना है' expresses an obligation or a task that needs completion. In English, 'have to' is the perfect choice for conveying external obligations, like a project with a deadline. We use 'have to' instead of 'must' because 'must' typically implies a stronger internal rule or personal necessity, whereas 'have to' fits perfectly for tasks driven by external requirements.
slides.hindiSummary: 'मुझे यह प्रोजेक्ट कल तक पूरा करना है' में 'करना है' बाहरी दायित्व को दर्शाता है, जिसके लिए 'have to' का प्रयोग उचित है।
